title: Why Do Farts Smell So Bad?
summary:
Why do farts smell so bad? Daisy, age 7, from New York, asked that question. A healthy person farts about 14 to 20 times a day -- enough gas to fill a stinky party balloon.

Farts are made by trillions of tiny living things called microbes, mostly bacteria, in your gut. They break down food your stomach cannot handle. As they work, they release gases that mix with air you swallow, then burst out as farts.

Most of a fart is odorless gas, mostly nitrogen. The stink comes from tiny amounts of gases that hold sulfur. One is hydrogen sulfide, which smells like rotten eggs. Another is methanethiol, which smells like cabbage or skunk spray. Just one hydrogen sulfide molecule in a million is enough to do the job.

What you eat changes the smell. Beans and grains can make farts bigger and louder. Meat, dairy, and eggs hold two sulfur amino acids, methionine and cysteine. Cabbage, broccoli, and cauliflower hold sulfur too. The loudest fart is not always the stinkiest. It is the sulfur that packs the smelly punch. Farting is useful too: it lets pressure out and stops painful bloating and cramping.
why_it_matters: Everyone farts every day, so knowing why it smells and why it helps your belly feel better can help you understand your own body.
